subject: Adaptive tier migration and addon alignment
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@wellpath.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Adaptive tier migration and addon alignment

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. We ran the internal post-mortem and want to move forward, but two questions before we commit: 1) Can you outline a safe migration path from our current composable setup to a simpler flat tier (we want predictable billing and fewer SKUs), and 2) how do you recommend handling the three addons we currently use (real-time embeddings, throughput burst, and private VPC export) so our legal and procurement teams can sign off without a huge amendment?

We have a pilot for June and would like pricing clarity by next week. Also attaching our current MA to this thread for reference (WellPath_MA_plan_v2.pdf).

Appreciate a succinct plan we can show procurement.

—Sara Kim
VP Product, WellPath Health
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@wellpath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-30T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Adaptive tier migration and addon alignment

Sara —

Appreciate the clarity. High level answer up front: yes, we can do a phased migration that preserves existing entitlements while moving billing to a flat-tier model, and we can bundle the three addons into a single "Managed Throughput" addon with an optional VPC export premium for regulated workloads.

Attached: redwood_pricing_matrix_2026.xlsx (high-level migration options + indicative pricing).

Brief proposed approach:
- Week 0 (alignment): sign migration addendum that pins current terms for 30 days while we run a pilot.
- Pilot (4–6 weeks): map current feature usage to flat-tier equivalents, enable a single Managed Throughput addon that covers burst + embeddings quota, and track delta via per-route metrics.
- Migration (post-pilot): transition billing to flat tier with a one-time conversion credit equal to unused committed tokens on current contract.

Concession note: for pilot customers we typically offer a one-time credit to smooth the step — we can discuss quantum with Ben (cc'd).

If you want, Ben and I can jump on a 30-min call with procurement this week to walk the proposal.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-30T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Adaptive tier migration and addon alignment — credit ask

Ben / Jordan — forwarding WellPath's ask. They want: predictable flat tier billing, consolidation of three addons into one bundle, and pricing clarity by next week because procurement needs it for the June pilot.

Key negotiation points:
- They expect a conversion credit for unused committed tokens.
- They will push for a pilot discount (we've done 10–20% historically).
- They care about not having a separate line-item for embeddings (security + audit reasons) — prefer a single addon.

Can you confirm what we can offer for: 1) conversion credit calculation (formula), 2) pilot discount band we can approve quick (no escalations), and 3) whether Managed Throughput addon can include VPC export at a single bundled price or we need to keep VPC as a premium?

Also flag any legal/open clause we should expect to include in the addendum. I would like to propose: 15% pilot discount + conversion credit = prorated unused committed tokens converted to 3 months of flat-tier credit.

—Lauren
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Adaptive tier migration and addon alignment — credit ask

Lauren —

Thanks. Quick answers:
1) Conversion credit: prorate remaining committed token value on a straight-line basis (remaining term value / remaining months * 3 months credit). Example in attached spreadsheet (redwood_pricing_matrix_2026.xlsx).
2) Pilot discount: we can approve up to 15% off list for pilots under $75k ARR without additional approval; 20% requires manager sign-off.
3) Managed Throughput addon: technically feasible to bundle embeddings + burst. VPC export touches compliance/KMS and should be treated as an opt-in premium unless the customer signs a higher support tier. However — for this deal we can include VPC export at a discounted pass-through fee for the pilot only (one-time).

Legal: include an explicit migration addendum that: (a) pins existing terms for pilot start date, (b) states conversion-credit formula, (c) defines the Managed Throughput SKU for pilot with automatic re-evaluation at pilot close. Procurement will like the explicit audit/data retention line.

If you want to hold margin, suggest we offer 15% pilot discount + 3-month conversion credit as you suggested, and keep VPC export as a $5k one-time premium during the pilot.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@wellpath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-01T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Adaptive tier migration and addon alignment — proposal and next steps

Sara —

Thanks again. We're aligned and can move fast. Summary of what we will put in the migration addendum for your procurement team:

1) Pilot setup (June start): 4–6 weeks, flat-tier pricing with a Managed Throughput addon that bundles real-time embeddings + throughput burst.
2) Pilot economics: 15% pilot discount on list for the pilot term.
3) Conversion credit: prorated unused committed tokens converted to a 3-month flat-tier credit (see enclosed example in redwood_pricing_matrix_2026.xlsx).
4) VPC export: available during pilot as a one-time $5,000 premium (discounted pass-through); if retained after pilot, it will be offered as a premium against the higher support tier or standalone add-on.
5) Legal: addendum will pin current terms for 30 days during the pilot and include audit/data retention language for compliance.

Next steps:
- I attached the pricing matrix and a short addendum draft for procurement (redwood_pricing_matrix_2026.xlsx).
- Can we schedule a 30-minute procurement sync Thursday 4/6 or Friday 4/7? If those don't work, propose two times and we'll accommodate.

If this looks good, I'll loop Jordan for the contract draft and Ben will prepare the pilot invoice.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
